sections.html:
A Texas City owner can list with an agent, take a cash offer, or negotiate an as-is deal. Houses with storm history, deferred repairs or title questions often suit a buyer who needs no mortgage. Your closing date, your loan payoff and what an inspector would find decide which route fits.

The city sits on the southwestern shore of Galveston Bay in Galveston County, and that shapes buyer questions. Water, drainage, insurance and roof age come up before paint colors do. Pulling your paperwork together early speeds up any route, and a short list is enough: the deed, a loan payoff, the latest tax bill and repair receipts.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, with inspections and lender timelines attached.
  • Cash sale as is: fewer contingencies and a closing date you choose.
  • Delayed closing: handy when you need time to move or to settle an estate.

sections.h2: Flood protection and the age of your house
sections.html:
Texas City grew quickly in the 1940s and 1950s, so many houses are decades old. Check your deed and permit records for the house's age and the work done on it.

After Hurricane Carla in 1961 put four feet of floodwater over much of the city, the response was physical: a barrier seawall begun in 1962 and finished in 1985, plus an eight-foot inner levee at Moses Lake built in 1982 with pumps. Local groundwater pumping ended because subsidence was adding to flooding. Buyers know this history, and they still ask whether your particular house has taken on water.

Work, schools and the water bring people in. Ten major refining and petrochemical industries form the base of the port, with growth running west from the bay. The Nessler Civic Center sits on a 55-acre tract that also holds the city's largest park, the library, city hall and the stadium. The Texas City Dike and Moses Lake handle recreation. College of the Mainland opened in September 1967.

  • Plant and port workers value a short drive to the job.
  • Commuters toward Houston or Galveston weigh an average trip of 25.7 minutes.
  • Families look at the school district and the parks.

Texas City had 59,733 residents in July 2025, 15.2 percent above the 2020 base. A growing city draws buyers, which helps a seller who prices in line with nearby sales.

Roughly 85 percent of residents stayed at the same address over the prior year. Long-tenured owners are common, and many hold older homes with plenty of equity and a long repair list.

Galveston Central Appraisal District values Texas City property. Its customer service office is at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, TX 77591. Hours run 7:30 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and until noon on Friday, and the phone is (409) 935-1980. Exemption applications can go in by mail, online or at the office, and GCAD acts within 90 days.

File a protest through the taxpayer portal, registering with the owner ID and eFile PIN from your notice. The online protest counts as your informal hearing. If you reach no agreement, the case goes to the appraisal review board.

  • The board meets in panels of three, and hearings typically run 15 to 20 minutes.
  • You can attend by phone or videoconference, send a written affidavit, or appear in person.
  • A final order comes by certified mail roughly three to four weeks later.
  • One reschedule is allowed for any reason, and hearings begin in May each year.

The filing deadline is May 15 or 30 days after your notice, whichever is later. An owner who wants to challenge the board's decision can choose binding arbitration or district court.

Bills go out around October 1. Anything unpaid by January 31 turns delinquent on February 1, and a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach. The lien dates to January 1, so your closing agent pays that year's tax before funding.

Qualifying homestead owners can get a school tax ceiling. A person with a disability can qualify under the Social Security definition even without receiving benefits. Call the Galveston County tax office for a payoff through your closing date.

sections.h2: Moving an exemption or tax ceiling
sections.html:
Maybe. A disabled owner's school tax ceiling can transfer as a percentage to a new qualifying Texas homestead. A ceiling for county, city or junior college taxes can move if you stay within the same taxing unit and that unit has adopted one. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older and keeps the home can continue the exemptions.

GCAD handles these exemption types: general residential, disabled person, age 65 or older, 100 percent disabled veteran, a donated residence of a partially disabled veteran, and surviving spouses of service members killed in action. Leaving for another Texas address? Ask GCAD about cancelling or porting an exemption before closing so the paperwork is in order.

sections.h2: Storm and condition records to assemble
sections.html:
Buyers here will put three questions to you: did the house ever take on water, what was fixed afterward, and what does insurance cover? Have written answers ready.

  • Insurance claim records, repair invoices and any elevation certificate you hold.
  • Photos of the roof, slab, drains and electrical panel.
  • Paperwork for any foundation work.
  • A check with the city permit office on whether past repairs were permitted.

A cash buyer taking the house as is will weigh these items in the price instead of demanding repairs. Records still help, because they shrink the unknowns a buyer would otherwise price in.

A foreclosure auction happens on a first Tuesday after 21 days' notice. Selling before that date can protect whatever equity you have. An inherited house needs someone with authority to sign, and a tenant is owed written notice to vacate before any court case.

Each of these starts with documents. For a lender problem, bring the default notice and loan statement. For an inheritance, bring the death certificate and any will. For a rental, bring the lease and the deposit record. A title company can then tell you how long clearing the file should take.

After a notary acknowledges your signature, the deed is filed with the Galveston County Clerk. Your title company usually takes care of that, and the closing statement shows any recording charges. Expect a final walk-through, keys handed over at funding, and a utility switch the same day. Photo ID is required at the table.

faqs.q: Must I repair storm damage before selling in Texas City?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer can take the house as is and price in the repairs. Disclose what you know and keep your invoices, since buyers ask.

faqs.q: Which office handles my Texas City appraisal?
faqs.a: Galveston Central Appraisal District, at (409) 935-1980 or at its Texas City office. The protest window runs to May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax on a Texas City sale?
faqs.a: Ask your title company. Recording fees and any other charges show up on your closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texas City house I inherited?
faqs.a: Often yes, once someone has authority to sign. A Texas probate attorney can confirm which paperwork you need.

faqs.q: How soon can a Texas City sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close as fast as the title work allows, often within a few weeks, while a financed sale depends on the lender. Liens and back taxes can slow either path.
